chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about the one in Ihram who is in need, so he finds the dead animal (carcass) and the hunted prey, which of these two should he eat? He said: He should eat from the hunted prey what he loves to eat from his own wealth. I said: Yes (why is that?). He said: Rather, upon him is the ransom, so let him eat and let him pay the ransom.

key_terms.الْمُحْرِمُ: One in the state of Ihram (ritual consecration)

ai.seo_question: What should a person in Ihram eat if they find both a dead animal and fresh prey out of necessity?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that a muhrim in dire need may consume hunted prey (samt) rather than carcass (maytah), treating it as consuming fresh meat from one's own wealth. However, this concession requires paying fidyah, highlighting the Shia juristic principle that the prohibition of hunting in Ihram is lifted under necessity but remains a compensable obligation. This ruling underscores the balance between preserving life and maintaining the sanctity of the pilgrimage state.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘

I asked himasws about the one in Ihraam being desperate, so he finds the dead (animal carcass), and the hunted prey, which of these two should he eat?’ Heasws said: ‘He should eat from the hunted prey what he loves to eat from his own wealth’. I said, ‘Why?’ Heasws said: ‘Rather, upon him is the ransom, so let him eat and let him (pay the) ransom’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabiy who has said the following: “I once asked abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man who faces an emergency and there are only carcasses and a prey. Which one can he eat? He (the Imam) said, ’He can eat from the prey as much as he likes to eat from his belongings? I then said, ‘Is it so?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘He only owes to pay ransom; he can eat and pay the ransom?”
